Subject: Exec approval request: Acme on-prem / audit-rights / discount

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick context: Acme (enterprise, healthcare vertical) is requesting a 12-month private/VPC deployment with on-prem-style audit rights. They want the ability to schedule red-team audits annually (limited to 2 days on-site and remote review otherwise), and an explicit clause requiring data residency in our US East deployment nodes. They also require a limited maintenance blackout window (Mon–Fri 9am–6pm ET) and a staff-maintenance-notification SLA of 72 hours.

Commercial ask: to win this we proposed a 35% first-year discount and a 12-month committed spend (they'll prepay 60% on signature). Deal economics: list price ARR would be $480k; with the discount ARR is $312k first year. I flagged this to Deal Desk and Legal — Rishi, Laura, can you confirm the workable risk posture on audit wording and the customer-facing remedy language?

Specific approvals needed from execs:
- One-time non-standard discount: 35% first year (exceeds standard discount cap of 25%)
- Approval for the limited on-prem audit carve-out (length and scope noted above) and acceptance of a written audit plan to be submitted 30 days in advance
- Approval to allow their KMS preference (they want to bring their own key but only within our HSM boundary with attestation; Legal note: will need an ARO)

Attachments: draft SOW with customer redlines (ACME_SOW_Redlines_v3.pdf), SOC2 summary they requested (SOC2_AuditSummary_2025.pdf), and pricing schedule (Pricing_MA_Schedule.xlsx).

I'm recommending we ask for the 35% discount conditional on: non-cancellable 12-month prepay of 60%, accepted SOW redlines limited to the audit schedule and blackout windows, and a risk mitigation addendum (we can require a separate security assessment paid by customer if audit goes beyond scope).

I can present the summary to leadership next week; please reply with redlines/objections. This is time sensitive — Acme wants signature by 2026-08-10 to hit their launch date.

Thanks,

Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. Quick legal/Deal Desk view from my side: the proposed discount (35%) exceeds our delegated approval thresholds; I will need an exec sign-off (CRO/CEO) for pricing outside policy. On the contractual asks:

1) Audit rights: Acceptable if we limit: (a) max two business days on-site per 12 months, (b) customer submits a detailed audit plan 30 days before, and (c) audit focused on access controls only — no source code or internal logs that contain other customers' metadata. We should also require an NDA addendum and an independent auditor if they push beyond scope.

2) Data residency: Fine to commit to US-only hosting for the customer if they accept a written SLA exception and we require a documented change request for any future movement.

3) BYOK/KMS: We'll accept customer-managed keys under the condition that keys remain in our supported HSM (no export), and we add an attestation clause confirming key control. Engineering will need to validate integration during onboarding; expect a 3–4 week lead time.

4) Maintenance blackout: We can include the blackout windows but want explicit permissible emergency maintenance carve-outs with notice and an SLA credit cap (we can propose a single-day credit per incident up to $X).

Operational mitigation recommended: require a security deposit (or holdback) tied to audit escalations and a cap on audit costs billed to customer beyond the two-day allowance.

I'm fine with us moving to execs for pricing approval provided Sales confirms the prepay and that the customer agrees to the proposed mitigations. Please prepare a one-page exec memo with the ask / opt-out conditions and projected ARR impact. I can draft the legal redline after we get sign-off.

Rgds,
Rishi
Senior Deal Desk Counsel | Redwood Inference
